chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the boundary of Jam' (the two narrow points). He said: 'What is between the two narrow points up to the valley of Muhassar.'

key_terms.الْمَأْزِمَيْنِ: The two narrow points (specifically referring to the narrow passages in the Valley of Mina)
key_terms.حَدِّ جَمْعٍ: The boundary of Jam' (the standing at two specific locations)
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّرٍ: The Valley of Muhassar, a specific location in Mina

ai.seo_question: What is the defined boundary for the ritual of Jam' in Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the precise geographical limits of the ritual 'Jam'' (standing) during Hajj, extending from the two narrow points (al-Ma'zimayn) to the Valley of Muhassar. It provides the physical framework for the Prophet's and Imams' practice of combining prayers, emphasizing the significance of the Muhassar valley as a key landmark in the Hajj itinerary. This definition ensures uniformity in ritual performance, linking the physical journey to the spiritual discipline of the pilgrim.
